d: Transfer ownership of a game to other Roblox users or groups.
h:
With game ownership transfer, you can transfer your games to groups you have publish access to. This unlocks all of the features available to groups, including permissions and revenue management, and allows you to efficiently manage your content as your team scales and your priorities shift.

Prerequisites

Before making a transfer or accepting a transfer, you must first:

  • Verify your email address.
  • Upload your private ModuleScripts and InsertService asset usages to the group you're transferring the game to. If the game uses packages where the package owner is a user and not a group, you might have to recreate those packages or replace them with packages that are already owned by a group.

If you use Open Cloud API keys for the game, be aware that the effective permissions of an API key are determined by the access of the user who last generated the API key. If the transfer changes that user's access to the game, the effective permissions of the API key change accordingly.

In many cases, transfers have no impact on existing API keys. For example, if you transfer a game from your user account to a group you own, your access stays equivalent and existing API keys continue to work as before.

If the transfer does change access, for instance, when you transfer to a group you do not own, or the original owner loses access, you should create new API keys under an account that has the appropriate access for the game.

Transfer a game

To transfer a game to a group:

  1. Go to Creations and choose the game you want to transfer.
  2. In the left-hand navigation, navigate to Publish Settings ⟩ Game details.
  3. Click Initiate ownership transfer.
  4. In the Transfer Details dialog, carefully read and acknowledge the implications of the transfer. Then, click Next.
  5. Select a group to transfer the game to. You must be able to publish games to this group.
  6. Verify the transfer by entering the game name.
  7. Click Initiate transfer. The Content Settings page updates to include the pending group's username.
Once the group accepts the transfer, Roblox revokes access to your game from the public, and closes all servers associated with the game. The transfer process typically completes in a few minutes but may take longer for complex games.
To cancel a pending transfer, click **Cancel transfer request** in the **Content Settings** page.

Receive a transferred game

To receive a transferred game:

  1. Go to the game page of the game you're receiving. You can navigate to this page by clicking the transfer request notification you received when the game's current owner initiated the transfer, or by directly getting the overview page link from the current owner.
  2. In the Transfer Details dialog, carefully read and acknowledge the implications of the transfer. Then, click Next.
  3. Verify the transfer by entering the game name.
  4. Click Accept transfer.
Once your group accepts the transfer, Roblox revokes access to your game from the public, and closes all servers associated with the game. The transfer process typically completes in a few minutes but may take longer for complex games.
  1. After the transfer to your group is complete, set up any new permissions you need and release the game to the public again.

Frequently asked questions

What kind of information does the transferred game retain?

The transferred game retains its old game ID, place ID, and URL.

Do transfer requests expire?

Yes, transfer requests expire after 7 days.

How often can the same game be transferred?

After receiving a transferred game, you must wait 30 days to transfer that game again.

Can changes be made to a game that's transferring?

You can continue making changes to the game until the new group owner accepts the transfer and the transfer process begins. Changes you make during the active transfer process specifically aren't carried over.

What happens to credit card information when a game is transferred?

Roblox removes credit card information when you transfer a game.

What happens to revenue from private server subscriptions when a game is transferred?

The group you transferred your game to receives the revenue from any existing private server subscriptions. This revenue does not respect any group or game revenue splitting.

New private server subscriptions respect revenue splitting.

Does transferring a game impact discovery?

Transferring a game doesn't impact search as long as the game's title remains the same, the new group owner is not a moderated account, and the game is released again after the transfer.

Note that transferring a game can impact discovery for up to 24 hours after the new group owner releases the game to the public again.

kid.simple: You can move a game you own into a Roblox group where you are allowed to publish. Groups have extra tools, like giving each teammate a role and splitting earnings, so this is handy when your project grows into a team. This page explains what to prepare, how to send the transfer, how the group accepts it, and what changes afterward. The big thing to know is that the game goes private and its servers close during the move, so you must release it again after.
kid.analogy: It is like moving your lemonade stand from your own driveway into a club you are part of. The stand keeps its name and spot, but now the club runs it, can assign jobs, and shares the money. While you move it, the stand is closed for a bit.
keyPoints: You can only transfer a game to a group you are allowed to publish games to.
Before transferring, verify your email and upload any private ModuleScripts and InsertService assets the game uses to the new group.
Packages owned by a person (not a group) may need to be remade or replaced with group-owned packages.
To send: Creations > your game > Publish Settings > Game details > Initiate ownership transfer, pick the group, type the game name, and click Initiate transfer.
To receive: open the game page from the notification, read and accept the details, type the game name, and click Accept transfer.
When the transfer is accepted, the game is made private and all its servers close. After it finishes, set permissions and release the game again.
The game keeps its game ID, place ID, and URL. Requests expire after 7 days, and a received game cannot be transferred again for 30 days.
Saved credit card information is removed, and changes you make during the active transfer are not kept.

terms.transfer: Moving ownership of the game from one owner to another. Here, from you to a group.
terms.group: A team account on Roblox that can own games and items. Members get roles that decide what they can do.
terms.publish access: Permission to publish games for a group. You need it to transfer a game to that group.
terms.ModuleScript: A script that holds code other scripts can load. If yours is private to your account, the group needs its own copy.
terms.InsertService: A service that loads assets into the game while it runs. Those assets must belong to the new owner for it to keep working.
terms.package: A reusable group of objects that can update everywhere at once. Its owner matters when the game changes hands.
terms.Open Cloud API key: A secret key that lets outside programs talk to your game. Its powers depend on the person who last made it, so it can stop working if that person loses access.
terms.revoke public access: Make the game private again so the public cannot join.
terms.revenue splitting: Sharing the money a game earns between group members or other groups by set percentages.
terms.private server subscriptions: Monthly payments players make to have their own server. Existing ones go to the new group without revenue splitting.

watchOut: Forgetting to release the game again after the transfer. It stays private until someone in the group releases it.
Making edits while the transfer is in progress. Those changes are not carried over, so wait until it finishes.
Not moving private ModuleScripts or person-owned packages first. Parts of the game can break because the group cannot load them.
Renaming the game around the transfer. Search is only unaffected if the title stays the same.
